Mark Carney says Canadian Ombudsperson for Responsible Enterprise office hasn’t been ‘effective’ since its 2019 setup

Canada is eliminating a watchdog that investigates alleged human rights violations committed by Canadian companies operating abroad, after Mark Carney said the office hadn’t been “effective” since it was set up in 2019.

The move comes as Canada faces criticism from Donald Trump’s administration over its “unacceptable” efforts to combat forced labour.

guardian.description:
Instructors hurled Maria Eduarda Rodrigues de Freitas into 40-metre abyss without attaching safety equipment

The American musician Oliver Tree has died in a helicopter crash in Brazil at the age of 32, according to reports.

Two helicopters collided over Rio de Janeiro on Sunday morning and crashed in the city’s western zone, killing all six people onboard, including Tree, several Brazilian media outlets reported.

Shirley Firth is hoping those responsible for Lindsay de Feliz’s death in 2019 will finally be convicted

Arrest of Min Zin, who writes about Myanmar and Chinese foreign policy, comes just month after Trump visit to Beijing

Min Zin was suspected of “engaging in espionage activities that endanger China’s national security,” China’s ministry of foreign affairs spokesperson, Lin Jian, said on Friday.

euronews.title: B-52 bomber crashes at Edwards Air Force Base in California
euronews.description: A B-52 Stratofortress went down at around 11:20 a.m. local time, with emergency crews scrambled to the scene. No casualty information has been released. The aircraft typically carries a crew of five.

euronews.title: 21-year-old woman dies after being launched off bridge without safety rope
euronews.description: Viral videos of the tragedy shared online show the anguish of onlookers when they realised the lady was launched off the Ponte do Esqueleto bridge in Brazil without the required safety rope. “She’s got no rope,” one witness to the accident is heard saying.

euronews.title: Meet Merlin: The duck that became the World Cup's viral mascot
euronews.description: A duck named Merlin has become an unlikely World Cup sensation after videos of him wearing a Mexico jersey and joining celebrations in Mexico City spread across social media.

euronews.title: Spain record surprising goalless draw against Cape Verde
euronews.description: Debutants Cape Verde, a nation of over 500,000 people, held out against Luis de la Fuente’s star-studded team, playing defensively and relying on few counterattacks that nearly caused an upset for Spain in the 90th.

euronews.title: 'Spider-Man of Yemen' dies after fall into volcanic crater
euronews.description: A Yemeni adventurer known online as the “Spider-Man of Yemen” died after falling into a volcanic crater while attempting a climb without safety equipment.

euronews.title: EU Commission expected to propose trade restriction options against Israeli settlements
euronews.description: The European Commission is expected to propose a range of options to restrict EU trade with Israeli settlements after member states piled on the pressure at a minister-level meeting on Monday.

euronews.title: EU fails to reach agreement on sanctioning Israel's Ben Gvir despite member state pressure
euronews.description: The bloc's foreign policy chief confirmed that discussions on restricting trade with illegal West Bank settlements will also continue ahead of July's ministerial meeting.

euronews.title: Suspected human-to-human sexual transmission of dermatophilosis
euronews.description: According to a study, sexual encounters in gay saunas in Lyon may have been responsible for the transmission. Antibiotic treatment led to a rapid improvement in patients’ condition.

euronews.title: Albania assures EU its Kushner-linked tourism project will meet environmental standards
euronews.description: Albania has promised that a €1.4bn project linked to Donald Trump's son-in-law will meet EU environmental standards, Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos said on Monday.

euronews.title: Two men convicted of arson plot targeting UK prime minister's properties
euronews.description: Two men face sentencing Friday after being found guilty of torching properties linked to the prime minister, in a case that has raised questions about foreign interference in British public life.

euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this June 15th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Moscow strike on Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra 'one of Russia’s most serious crimes against Christian culture'
euronews.description: The Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra, one of the most important historic and religious symbols of Ukraine, has been hit in Moscow's drone and missile attack overnight on Monday, in what President Zelenskyy has called “one of Russia’s most serious crimes against Christian culture to date.”

euronews.title: From energy corridors to AI: Can the Turkic world become a new economic force?
euronews.description: Turkic states met in Shusha this weekend to boost competition law, digital cooperation and trade, aiming to align antitrust rules and strengthen regional connectivity.

euronews.title: Czech government scraps licence fees for public media in move critics call threat to press freedom
euronews.description: The right-wing populist coalition of Prime Minister Andrej Babiš has approved a bill replacing the traditional funding model with direct state financing, triggering strikes and protests.

euronews.title: Ukraine and Moldova press ahead with bid to join the EU on enlargement ‘Mega Monday’
euronews.description: In what’s been hailed by the European Union’s enlargement chief as ‘Mega Monday’, Ukraine and Moldova are breaking a two-year political deadlock by formally kicking off the first phase of negotiations on joining the bloc.

euronews.title: Voices of Pride: European celebrities advocating for LGBTQIA+ rights
euronews.description: Pride Month, celebrated every June, shines a spotlight on LGBTQIA+ people, their achievements, and the challenges they continue to face. While support for the community often becomes more visible during this time of year, many public figures advocate for LGBTQIA+ rights year-round.

euronews.title: Athens classics summit targets modern crises with ancient philosophy
euronews.description: The Second World Conference of Classics in Athens has concluded with the adoption of a joint declaration, establishing a structured framework to apply Greco-Roman and Chinese philosophical traditions to contemporary geopolitical and technological crises.

euronews.title: Lavender Provence farmers forced to raise laying hens to keep their activity going
euronews.description: The emblem of Provence, which attracts thousands of tourists every year, isn't as profitable as before. Lavender has become a burden for many farmers who are operating at a loss and choose to diversify to survive.

rfi.title: Journalists disappear as intimidation grips Mozambique's Cabo Delgado region
rfi.description: Almost a decade after an Islamist insurgency erupted in Mozambique's northern Cabo Delgado province, few reports on the conflict are emerging from the region. This third instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories, to which RFI contributed – hears from journalists and activists facing intimidation and violence.

rfi.title: France's Macron warns Iran against imposing Hormuz tolls
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday warned Iran against imposing tolls on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, saying "everything" should be done so fees are not charged for passage through the key bottleneck.

rfi.title: US and Iran reach deal to end war, reopen Hormuz
rfi.description: The United States and Iran said they reached a deal to end the Middle East war on all fronts including Lebanon, and reopen the vital Strait of Hormuz, but offered little indication on the thorny question of Tehran's nuclear programme.

rfi.title: NGO warns Ebola epidemic is 'outpacing' response efforts in DRC
rfi.description: French NGO Doctors Without Borders warned Monday that "dangerous gaps" remain in efforts to rein in an Ebola outbreak that has killed more than 180 people in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Since the first reported cases a month ago, the virus has spread rapidly, with the situation now critical in Ituri province.

rfi.title: ‘No blank cheque' for president or government says Senegal’s Sonko
rfi.description: In his first major international interview since becoming Speaker of Senegal's National Assembly, former prime minister Ousmane Sonko talks to RFI and sister channel France 24 about his split with his long-time ally President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. In the wide-reaching discussion, he also touches on the debt crisis, homosexuality legislation, regional security, his political aspirations and the World Cup.

rfi.title: First contact: Cape Verde's rise to the global stage
rfi.description: Cape Verde will make its World Cup debut at the 2026 tournament in the United States, Mexico and Canada. In the third instalment of a four-part series, RFI looks at the journey of the second smallest nation after Curaçao to qualify for the competition in its 96-year history.

rfi.title: Macron leads effort to bridge divides with Trump at France's G7 summit
rfi.description: As a G7 summit opens in eastern France on Monday, President Emmanuel Macron is set to lead the allies' efforts to narrow differences with the United States on Iran, Ukraine, trade and big tech regulation.

rfi.title: Cameroon opposition figure files complaint in France against President Biya
rfi.description: Former Cameroonian presidential candidate Issa Tchiroma Bakary says he's filed two complaints with the Paris Judicial Court against President Paul Biya, citing the principle of universal jurisdiction.

rfi.title: Clashes as thousands protest in Geneva ahead of G7 summit in France
rfi.description: Protesters in Geneva threw stones and firecrackers at the police, who responded with tear gas and water cannons during a demonstration Sunday against the G7 summit in nearby Evian.

rfi.title: Somaliland president makes 'historic' visit to Israel
rfi.description: Somaliland's President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi met his Israeli counterpart on Sunday in Jerusalem in his first-ever state visit, which comes months after Israel officially recognised the breakaway African state.

rfi.title: UK intercepts Russian shadow fleet vessel in Channel: ministry
rfi.description: British forces on Sunday intercepted a sanctioned oil tanker belonging to Russia's shadow fleet in the English Channel, the defence ministry said, in a six-hour operation hailed by Kyiv.

rfi.title: The project nurturing West Africa's new generation of women filmmakers
rfi.description: Some of the West African film industry's biggest names are backing a new mentorship programme to support emerging women filmmakers. Showcased at this year's Cannes Film Festival, the Mariama Lab project aims to help women bring their stories to a wider audience in the region and beyond.

rfi.title: Ghana lodges protest over Canada's refusal to admit rape case suspect Partey
rfi.description: Ghana's government confirmed on Saturday it had lodged a formal protest with Canada over its refusal to issue an entry visa to the Ghana midfielder Thomas Partey ahead of Ghana's game against Panama on Wednesday in Toronto.

rfi.title: South Africa accused of failing to crack down on anti-immigrant violence
rfi.description: Several African countries are repatriating their citizens from South Africa following weeks of xenophobic attacks on black migrants. The vigilante violence has drawn international condemnation, with some accusing the South African authorities of failing to take a tough approach.

rfi.title: Uganda's Ghetto Kids to shake it with Shakira at World Cup final
rfi.description: A group of young Ugandan dancers from the slums of Kampala have been invited to perform alongside pop star Shakira at the 2026 World Cup final, an opportunity they hope will bring them new visibility and help them transform their future.

rfi.title: US boss Pochettino hails sweep past Paraguay to launch World Cup campaign
rfi.description: United States head coach Mauricio Pochettino lavished praise on his players and the American fans after his side romped past Paraguay 4-1 at the Los Angeles Stadium.

rfi.title: Whistleblowing is on the rise in France, but expert says support remains lacking
rfi.description: Whistleblowing in France is on the rise, according to the independent authority in charge of protecting those who speak out in the public interest. The Défenseur des Droits has seen an increase in cases, reflecting a growing awareness of the process of speaking out and the protection available for those who do.

rfi.title: Resumption of $20bn Cabo Delgado gas project reignites both hope and resentment
rfi.description: The resumption of one of the world's biggest gas projects by French energy giant TotalEnergies, after a five-year suspension following a deadly jihadist attack, has raised hopes of jobs and prosperity in northern Mozambique. But this second instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories, to which RFI contributed – questions whether the country's vast gas wealth will benefit local communities.

lemonde.title: « L’abîme est béant » : la puissance militaire et l’impasse stratégique d’Israël après l’accord entre les Etats-Unis et l’Iran
lemonde.description: Alors que l’Etat hébreu avait pour objectif l’élimination de la « menace existentielle » du régime iranien, il a été tenu à l’écart du protocole d’accord conclu dimanche entre les Etats-Unis et l’Iran, tandis que son armée risque de perdre sa liberté d’action au Liban.

lemonde.title: G7 à Evian : l’activisme diplomatique d’Emmanuel Macron à l’épreuve des fragilités sur le plan national
lemonde.description: Englué dans une fin de mandat complexe en France, en pleine affaire Lyhanna, le chef de l’Etat, qui préside le sommet du G7 à Evian, mise tout sur son agenda international pour regagner une légitimité.

lemonde.title: A Kiev, une frappe a endommagé la cathédrale de la Dormition, au cœur de l’historique laure des Grottes
lemonde.description: Les responsables ukrainiens accusent la Russie de cibler délibérément des lieux culturels symbolisant l’identité ukrainienne, alors que des bombardements intenses ont touché le pays dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi.

lemonde.title: Mort de Lyhanna : de nouveaux rassemblements devant le ministère de la justice et les tribunaux ont eu lieu lundi soir
lemonde.description: Les révélations concernant les signalements et les plaintes pour viols sur mineures qui visaient le suspect dans la mort de Lyhanna, collégienne de 11 ans, ont suscité une vive émotion et relancé le débat sur les défaillances judiciaires.

lemonde.title: Enki Bilal, auteur de BD : « Ceux qui me disent que ce que je faisais avant était mieux ne savent pas lire »
lemonde.description: « Dans ma bulle ». L’auteur a ouvert jeudi 11 juin un fonds consacré à son œuvre dans le quartier du Marais, à Paris. Les planches originales, dessins, peintures, sculptures et films exposés mettent en valeur un travail protéiforme, en perpétuelle évolution.

lemonde.title: Belgique-Egypte : les Diables rouges et les Pharaons se quittent sur un score de parité
lemonde.description: Pour leur premier match dans le tournoi, les Belges de Kevin De Bruyne ont été longtemps menés par Mohamed Salah et ses coéquipiers. Romelu Lukaku leur a permis d’accrocher le match nul, quelques secondes après son entrée en jeu.

lemonde.title: Le Parlement entérine la restitution à la Guyane des restes de six Amérindiens, exhibés dans des « zoos humains »
lemonde.description: En 1892, 33 Amérindiens furent emmenés par paquebot vers l’Hexagone et exhibés vivants dans des « zoos humains » au Jardin d’acclimatation, à Paris. Huit d’entre eux ne survécurent pas.

lemonde.title: Allergies : la chaleur et la pollution augmentent la sensibilité dans la population
lemonde.description: La saison des graminées bat son plein, bientôt remplacée par celle de l’ambroisie. En France, plus du quart de la population souffre d’allergies, une part qui grandit sous l’effet du réchauffement climatique et des modifications environnementales.

lemonde.title: Huit personnes présumées mortes dans le crash d’un bombardier B-52 en Californie
lemonde.description: L’avion s’est écrasé peu après son décollage « lors d’une mission d’essai de routine en Californie », selon la base aérienne d’Edwards, où l’accident dramatique s’est produit.

lemonde.title: Israël : Benyamin Nétanyahou annonce être candidat aux prochaines élections législatives
lemonde.description: « Je vais me présenter aux élections et j’ai l’intention de gagner », a déclaré le dirigeant, lundi soir, au cours de sa première prise de parole depuis que Washington et Téhéran ont conclu un accord visant à mettre fin à la guerre dans la région.

lemonde.title: Ousmane Sonko, ancien premier ministre du Sénégal : « Nous n’avons pas de leçons à recevoir de l’étranger »
lemonde.description: Trois semaines après avoir été remercié de son poste de chef du gouvernement, Ousmane Sonko, désormais président de l’Assemblée nationale, livre, dans un entretien au « Monde », son analyse de la situation politique au Sénégal, après deux ans d’exercice du pouvoir.

lemonde.title: L’œuvre de JR, « La Caverne du Pont-Neuf », ouvre au public à Paris, jusqu’au 28 juin
lemonde.description: L’ouverture au public devait initialement débuter le 6 juin, mais elle a été reportée en raison de déchirures dans la structure gonflable qui surplombe le pont provoquées par de fortes rafales de vent quatre jours plus tôt.

lemonde.title: Autonomie de la Corse : le projet de réforme constitutionnelle arrive à l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Première étape d’un parcours législatif qui s’annonce incertain, le projet de loi constitutionnelle « pour une Corse autonome au sein de la République » doit être discuté en séance publique à l’Assemblée nationale, à partir du mardi 16 juin.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump annonce un meeting politique le 4 juillet, pour la fête nationale et le 250ᵉ anniversaire des États-Unis
lemonde.description: Après des combats de MMA à la Maison Blanche, le président américain entend réunir ses soutiens dans la capitale pour un meeting d’ampleur le jour de la fête nationale, traditionnellement célébrée hors des clivages partisans.

lemonde.title: Avoir une « bonne conduite » devient une condition pour vivre en Suède
lemonde.description: Lundi, les députés ont adopté un projet de loi qui fait de la « conduite » des ressortissants étrangers une condition pour l’octroi d’un titre de séjour. La mesure est dénoncée par de nombreuses organisations, qui y voient une menace pour la liberté d’expression et de manifestation.

lemonde.title: Mahmoud Abbas, le dirigeant de l’Autorité palestinienne, annonce une élection présidentielle au début de 2027
lemonde.description: Elu en 2005 après la mort du premier président de l’Autorité palestinienne, Yasser Arafat, Mahmoud Abbas n’a pas dit s’il serait candidat à sa propre succession. Des élections législatives se tiendront également en fin d’année prochaine.

zeit.description: Die deutsche Raumfahrtfirma Isar Aerospace hat kurz vor einem geplanten Testflug eine Fehlfunktion entdeckt. Die Nachfrage nach der Rakete Spectrum ist trotzdem groß.

zeit.description: Gavin Newsom berichtet von Befragungen von Familienmitgliedern, Freunden und Ex-Mitarbeitern. Kaliforniens Gouverneur sieht darin einen Rachefeldzug des US-Präsidenten.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : Lamouchi remercié ? L'avenir du sélectionneur de la Tunisie en suspens
france24fr.description: L'avenir du sélectionneur de la Tunisie, Sabri Lamouchi, fait l'objet de "discussions entre membres du bureau fédéral", a fait savoir lundi en fin d'après-midi une source proche du dossier. Ces soubresauts sur le banc tunisien font suite à la lourde défaite des Aigles de Carthage face à la Suède (5-1) lors de leur premier match du Mondial 2026.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : 782 cas confirmés d'Ebola et deux nouvelles zones affectées, MSF s'inquiète
france24fr.description: L'épidémie d'Ebola en RDC : MSF tire la sonnette d'alarme. L'ONG s'inquiète des « dangereuses lacunes » dans la réponse sanitaire alors que l'épidémie se diffuse plus rapidement que les capacités de réponse mises en œuvre sur le terrain. Notre envoyée spéciale à Bunia a pu se rendre dans un hôpital.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : comment la FIFA justifie les tribunes vides
france24fr.description: Les images de tribunes clairsemées lors du match qui a opposé la Corée du Sud à la République Tchèque en phase de poules du Mondial ont relancé la polémique sur les prix des billets jugés exorbitants. La FIFA s'est expliquée quant aux photos et aux vidéos de sièges vides, en se défendant de tout échec lié à sa billetterie.

france24fr.title: Avec l'accord Iran-Etats-Unis, soudaine détente sur les prix du pétrole
france24fr.description: A peine l'annonce d'un accord de paix a-t-elle eu lieu que les marchés ont respiré un grand coup. Les bourses ont toutes passées la séance dans le vert alors que le pétrole, WTI américain ou Brent de la mer du nord entamaient une chute de 5% environ, les plaçant aux alentours de 80 dollars le baril. Pour les marchés, échaudés par le record de 120 dollars le baril atteint en avril, c'est la détente; les entreprises de l'aéronautique ou de l'automobile ont vu leurs actions s'apprécier franchement.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Belgique et l'Égypte se neutralisent au terme d'une rencontre animée
Mondial 2026 : la Belgique et l'Égypte se neutralisent au terme d'une rencontre intense
france24fr.description: La Belgique et l'Égypte n'ont pas réussi à se départager (1-1), lundi, lors du premier match du groupe G du Mondial 2026. Les Diables Rouges ont longtemps couru après le score face à des Pharaons réalistes, mais l'entrée de Lukaku a été décisive pour obtenir le point du nul.

france24fr.title: États-Unis-Iran : une paix possible ?
france24fr.description: L’accord entre Washington et Téhéran, qui doit être signé vendredi à Genève, prévoit la réouverture du détroit d’Ormuz et la fin du blocus américain sur les ports iraniens. Il inclut aussi un cessez le feu de 60 jours pendant lequel les deux parties négocieront sur le nucléaire et la levée des sanctions sur l’Iran. Mais cet accord, qui laisse de côté de nombreuses questions dont la fin des opérations israéliennes au Liban voulue par Téhéran, reste bien fragile...

france24fr.title: Belgique - Égypte : les Diables Rouges et les Pharaons se quittent dos à dos
france24fr.description: La Belgique et l'Égypte se sont neutralisées, lundi soir, pour le premier match du groupe G du Mondial 2026. Les Diables Rouges ont longtemps subi face à des Pharaons réalistes, mais l'entrée de Lukaku leur a redonné de l'espoir. Revivez la rencontre grâce à notre direct commenté.

france24fr.title: Réchauffement climatique: le seuil de +1,5°C bientôt atteint
france24fr.description: Un groupe de 70 scientifiques à produit un rapport pour mettre à jour nos connaissances sur l'évolution du changement climatique. Selon leurs calculs, nous allons franchir la barre d'1,5°C de réchauffement climatique autour de 2030. Leur message: il y a urgence à réduire nos émissions de gaz à effet de serre pour préserver un climat vivable et réduire le nombre de catastrophes qui nous attendent si nous restons sur la trajectoire actuelle de +3°C à la fin du XXIè siècle.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : un valeureux Cap-Vert crée l'exploit et tient l'Espagne en échec
Mondial 2026 : un valeureux Cap-Vert crée l'exploit et tient l'Espagne en échec
france24fr.description: L'Espagne a manqué ses débuts à la Coupe du monde, lundi, avec un match nul face au Cap-Vert (0-0), à Atlanta. La Roja a eu de multiples occasions mais a buté sur des Requins Bleus valeureux, à commencer par leur gardien Vozinha auteur de plusieurs arrêts décisifs.

france24fr.title: G7 : l'accord iranien en toile de fond
france24fr.description: Donald Trump est arrivé à Evian pour le G7 alors que l'accord de paix avec l'Iran vient d'être conclu. Il inclut notamment la réouverture du détroit d'Ormuz et un cessez-le-feu de 60 jours pendant lesquels les deux parties vont négocier sur la question du nucléaire et sur la levée des sanctions sur l'Iran. Les explications avec Sébastien Boussois, chercheur spécialiste du Moyen-Orient et des Relations internationales, rédacteur en chef de l’hebdo belge « Pan ».

france24fr.title: Brésil: une femme meurt lors d'un saut dans le vide après un oubli de sécurité
france24fr.description: Une femme de 21 ans est décédée au Brésil lors d’un “rope jump,” une discipline proche du saut à l’élastique. Sur une vidéo filmée par des témoins on la voit se faire jeter d’un pont, par deux hommes, pour un saut dans le vide mais sans corde  de sécurité. Trois hommes ont été arrêtés pour homicide.

france24fr.title: Ces images ne montrent pas un hélicoptère français abattu à la frontière du Mali
france24fr.description: Des internautes sympathisants de l’Alliance des États du Sahel (AES) affirment qu’un hélicoptère français transportant des terroristes aurait été abattu à la frontière du Mali. Mais parmi les images présentées comme preuve, l'une montre un aéronef américain et d’autres sont probablement issues d’un jeu vidéo.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : l'Espagne entre en lice face au Cap-Vert
france24fr.description: L'Espagne, l'un des favoris du Mondial 2026, fait son entrée dans la Coupe du Monde, lundi, face au Cap-Vert. Le Petit Poucet de la compétition dispute sa première Coupe du monde et aura fort à faire face à une Roja attendue.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : l’équipe du Sénégal s'entraîne à J-2 de son match avec la France
france24fr.description: Les joueurs de l'équipe du Sénégal s'entraînent deux jours avant leur premier match de Coupe du monde 2026 contre la France. Il y a 24 ans, lors de leur dernière rencontre, les Lions de la Teranga avaient créé la surprise générale en battant les Bleus, alors tenants du titre.

france24fr.title: L'Ukraine entame son très long chemin vers une adhésion à l'Union européenne
france24fr.description: L'Ukraine a franchi lundi une étape importante pour son adhésion à l'UE avec le lancement d'une première série de négociations devant conduire Kiev à s'aligner sur les standards européens en matière d'environnement, d'agriculture ou encore de marché intérieur. Un processus long et complexe, rendu encore plus difficile par la guerre en cours contre la Russie.

france24fr.title: Protocole d'accord au Moyen-Orient : "L’Iran a tenu tête et imposé son calendrier et ses conditions"
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis et l’Iran ont conclu dimanche un protocole d’accord visant à mettre fin à la guerre au Moyen-Orient, incluant la réouverture du détroit d’Ormuz, la levée du blocus américain et l'arrêt immédiat des opérations militaires sur tous les fronts, y compris au Liban. Un cadre de négociations perçu par de nombreux observateurs comme largement favorable à Téhéran.

nzz.description: Vom 15. bis 17. Juni findet in Évian auf der französischen Seite des Genfersees der G-7-Gipfel statt. In Genf wurde am Sonntag gegen die Veranstaltung demonstriert, teilweise mit Gewalt.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Trumps zweite Amtszeit: Kongress verabschiedet Milliarden für Einwanderungsbehörde ICE – Erfolg für Trump
nzz.description: Donald Trump regiert zum zweiten Mal als amerikanischer Präsident – mit weitreichenden innen- und aussenpolitischen Folgen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: Hormuz, Handel, Helvetia – Trump und Iran stellen den G-7-Gipfel auf den Kopf
nzz.description: Die Aussicht auf ein Iran-Abkommen verändert die Agenda des G-7-Gipfels. Emmanuel Macron hofft auf diplomatischen Schwung und versucht, Donald Trump weiter bei Laune zu halten. Ärger über ein altes Problem gibt es zudem mit den Schweizer Nachbarn.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Trumps löchriges Abkommen mit Iran: Im Nahen Osten wird es unruhig bleiben
nzz.description: Der amerikanische Präsident wollte Geschichte schreiben: das Regime in Teheran stürzen oder zumindest sein Atom- und Raketenprogramm sowie die Unterstützung für ausländische Milizen stoppen. Nun endet der Krieg vorerst in einer vagen Einigung.

nzz.title: Niederlage für Bundesrat Albert Rösti: Das AKW-Verbot bleibt, zumindest vorläufig
nzz.description: Äusserst knapp hat der Nationalrat beschlossen, den indirekten Gegenvorschlag zur sogenannten Blackoutinitiative zurück an den Bundesrat zu weisen. Entscheidend war die Mitte-Partei, die das AKW-Verbot einst initiierte.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Die EU-Beitrittsverhandlungen mit der Ukraine haben begonnen +++ Neue Sanktionen gegen Russlands Kriegswirtschaft
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Neuigkeiten im Überblick.

nzz.title: Offene Fragen in Trumps Iran-Deal lösen in den USA Skepsis aus
nzz.description: Der amerikanische Präsident setzt darauf, dass die Inflation nach der Öffnung der Strasse von Hormuz sinkt. Dennoch ist das Rahmenabkommen mit Teheran innenpolitisch nicht leicht zu verkaufen.

nzz.title: Verspätete Flüge, teure Familientarife: Flugpassagiere in der EU und in der Schweiz erhalten mehr Rechte
nzz.description: Fluggesellschaften werben oft mit intransparenten Tarifen. Zudem handhaben sie Entschädigungen bei Verspätungen unterschiedlich. Der Wildwuchs soll nun ein Ende haben. Schweizer profitieren dank den bilateralen Verträgen.

nzz.title: Vor Trump taumelt blutüberströmt der Star des Abends: Der Käfigkampf beim Weissen Haus bietet ein surreales Spektakel
nzz.description: Fans des brutalen Vollkontaktsports bekamen einen herausragenden Titelkampf zu sehen. Doch die fünfstündige Veranstaltung fordert nicht nur unzählige Platzwunden, sie verlangt auch Sitzfleisch. Und für Kritiker des Präsidenten markiert sie eine Rückkehr zur Barbarei.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - KI in Politik und Medien: wie man es nicht machen sollte
nzz.description: Der Springer-Chef Mathias Döpfner desavouiert mit einer KI-Demonstration seine besten Schreiber. Das ist nicht nur widersprüchlich, sondern ignoriert auch, dass der politische Diskurs eine Seele braucht.

nzz.title: Das Genfer Stimmvolk verbietet gewählten Volksvertreterinnen das Kopftuch
nzz.description: Die Genferinnen und Genfer fordern von ihren kantonalen und kommunalen Mandatsträgern Neutralität hinsichtlich ihrer Religion. Doch noch ist nichts entschieden, die Justiz wurde eingeschaltet.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die jüngsten Entwicklungen des Ukraine-Krieges in Bildern
nzz.description: Die russische Invasion hat Millionen von Ukrainerinnen und Ukrainern in die Flucht getrieben. Während der Abnutzungskrieg unerbittlich weitergeht, droht Kiew durch die aussenpolitische Neuausrichtung von US-Präsident Donald Trump weiter unter Druck zu geraten. Die aktuellen Entwicklungen in Bildern.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Die USA und Iran verkünden ein Abkommen: die Übersicht
nzz.description: In der Nacht zum 15. Juni 2026 haben sich die USA und Iran auf die Rahmenbedingungen für ein Friedensabkommen geeinigt. Das Abkommen beendet oder pausiert zumindest die gefährliche Phase einer militärischen Eskalation im Nahen Osten.

spiegel.title: Wadephul nennt Bedingungen für deutschen Militäreinsatz in Straße von Hormus
spiegel.description: Streitkräfte aus Europa sollen sich an einer sicheren Öffnung der Meerenge zwischen Iran und Oman beteiligen. Doch Deutschlands Außenminister Johann Wadephul zeigt sich zurückhaltend.

spiegel.title: USA: B-52-Langstrecken-Bomber der US-Streitkräfte in Kalifornien abgestürzt
spiegel.description: Bei der Edwards Air Force Base in der kalifornischen Mojave-Wüste ist ein Langstreckenbomber vom Typ B-52 zerschellt. Bilder zeigen, wie Rauch über verkohlter Erde aufsteigt. Offenbar starben acht Menschen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Romelu Lukaku erzwingt Belgiens Ausgleich gegen Ägypten nach Einwechslung
spiegel.description: Die goldene Generation der Belgier ist älter geworden, aber immer noch brandgefährlich. Beim Gegner stand Geburtstagskind Mohamed Salah im Fokus.

spiegel.title: Isar Aerospace: Münchner Raumfahrt-Start-up sagt erneut Startversuch ab
spiegel.description: Mehrfach sind Testflüge des deutschen Raumfahrtunternehmen Isar Aerospace in diesem Jahr bereits gescheitert. Der für Montagabend geplante Start musste nun ebenfalls abgesagt werden.

spiegel.title: Gavin Newsom wirft Donald Trump vor, gegen ihn zu ermitteln
spiegel.description: Beamte sollen sich durch Berge von Akten gewühlt haben: Kaliforniens Gouverneur sagt, die Trump-Regierung habe eine politisch motivierte Untersuchung gegen ihn aufgenommen. Auch seine Frau sei ins Visier der Ermittler geraten.

spiegel.title: Stephan-Andreas Casdorff: »Jüdische Allgemeine« entfernt wegen KI-Verdacht zwei Kommentare von Ex-»Tagesspiegel«-Chefredakteur
spiegel.description: Der frühere »Tagesspiegel«-Herausgeber Stephan-Andreas Casdorff soll auch zwei Gastkommentare von einer KI generiert haben lassen. Zwei Beiträge in der »Jüdische Allgemeinen« stehen unter Verdacht, der Chefredakteur kündigt strengere Regeln an.

spiegel.title: Bonnie Tyler nach fünf Wochen aus Koma erwacht
spiegel.description: Die britische Popsängern Bonnie Tyler ist nicht mehr im künstlichen Koma. Sie ist aber nach wie vor schwer krank. Ihre Konzerte im Sommer hat ihr Management nun abgesagt.

spiegel.title: Polen: Ärztin soll mehr als 30 menschliche Föten im Garten vergraben haben
spiegel.description: Bauarbeiter haben in einem Dorf in Polen einen grausigen Fund gemacht: 34 menschliche Föten sollen in einem Garten vergraben gewesen sein. Festgenommen wurde nun eine Ärztin.

spiegel.title: Marius Borg Høiby kommt nicht aus Untersuchungshaft frei
spiegel.description: Der Sohn von Norwegens Kronprinzessin Mette-Marit bleibt auch nach seiner Verurteilung in Untersuchungshaft, ein Antrag von ihm wurde abgelehnt. Zu hoch sei das Risiko neuer Gewalttaten gegen seine Ex-Freundin.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: EU beginnt Verhandlungen zum Ukrainebeitritt
spiegel.description: Nach der zweijährigen Hängepartie hat die Europäische Union am Montag die Beitrittsverhandlungen mit der Ukraine eröffnet. Dabei soll es zunächst um Themen wie das Justizsystem, Grundwerte und Sicherheit gehen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Gegen Spanien – Kap Verde sorgt für eine der größten Sensationen der WM-Geschichte
spiegel.description: Kap Verde ist zum ersten Mal bei einer WM-Endrunde, der Linksverteidiger spielte vor Kurzem noch bei Viktoria Köln. Nun blamierte der Inselstaat Europameister Spanien. Daran konnte auch Lamine Yamal nichts ändern.

spiegel.title: Russland-Ukraine-Krieg: Lawra in Kyjiw – ein Heiligtum in Flammen
spiegel.description: Die Lawra in Kyjiw gehört zu den wichtigsten Heiligtümern der Ukraine. Während einer Serie russischer Luftschläge wurde das Gelände des berühmten Höhlenklosters beschädigt, die Hauptkirche geriet in Brand. Was darüber bekannt ist.

spiegel.title: USA-Iran-Einigung: Plötzlich steht Benjamin Netanyahu als Verlierer da
spiegel.description: Das Abkommen der USA mit Iran wird in Israel als Katastrophe gesehen. Die Partnerschaft zwischen Netanyahu und Trump ist wohl beendet.

spiegel.title: Hamburg: Frühere Parteispitze der Grünen zahlt Sozialabgaben nach
spiegel.description: Bei den Hamburger Grünen rumorte es, weil Sozialversicherungsbeiträge ausstanden. Nun zahlt die ehemalige Landesspitze der Partei offenbar selbst den ausstehenden Betrag, obwohl die Partei die Kosten eigentlich übernehmen wollte.

spiegel.title: Wohnungskrise in Spanien: Rausschmeißer vs. Hausbesetzer - SPIEGEL TV für Arte Re
spiegel.description: Immer wieder besetzen Menschen Häuser und Wohnungen in Spanien. Die Rechtslage ist komplex und Gerichtsverfahren langwierig. Viele Eigentümer engagieren daher private Räumungsfirmen. Eine »Arte Re:«-Reportage von SPIEGEL TV.

spiegel.title: »Gut genug«: Wird Shirin David von Heidi Klum gedisst?
spiegel.description: Model Heidi Klum versucht sich manchmal im Singen – mit bescheidenem Ergebnis. Das hindert die Entertainerin aber nicht daran, ihre Meinung zu Shirin Davids viralem Sommerhit kundzutun.

spiegel.title: Krieg in Iran: Donald Trump hat Iran-Abkommen offenbar digital unterschrieben
spiegel.description: US-Regierungskreisen zufolge ist die Friedensvereinbarung mit Iran bereits digital unterschrieben worden. Die USA sollen Iran zudem 300 Milliarden Dollar für den Wiederaufbau in Aussicht gestellt haben.

spiegel.title: Ungarn: Parlament verhindert mögliche Wiederwahl von Viktor Orbán
spiegel.description: Mit einer Änderung seiner Verfassung hat das ungarische Parlament die Amtszeit des Ministerpräsidenten auf acht Jahre begrenzt. Damit kann der abgewählte Rechtspopulist Orbán nicht erneut kandidieren.

arxiv-ai.description:

Abstract: The Muddy Children Puzzle is a puzzle about knowledge and ignorance that has been inspiring for the development of epistemic logic. Who came up with it first? This is unclear. We trace the origin of the Muddy Children Puzzle through logical and literary publications over the past two centuries. The puzzle inspired a numerous variations such as involving numbers or coloured hats. We also present a novel hats puzzle involving self-reference.

phys-org.title: New imaging technique measures single scramblase proteins, revealing lipid transport rates
phys-org.description: A new single-protein analysis technique gives researchers an unprecedented ability to study proteins called scramblases, which have critical roles in biology. The development of the new technique, in a study led by investigators at Weill Cornell Medicine and Ruhr University Bochum in Germany, expands the toolkit available to cell biologists and biophysicists and could someday be useful in devising new strategies against multiple diseases.

phys-org.title: International surrogates recruited on social media face emotional control in Georgia's booming childbirth market
phys-org.description: Since 2022, Georgia's surrogacy industry has boomed, with oversubscribed clinics now recruiting women from across Central Asia via Instagram and TikTok. New research conducted at the University of Oxford's Centre on Migration, Policy and Society (COMPAS) provides unprecedented insight into the hidden systems of emotional control sustaining Georgia's transnational surrogacy market.

phys-org.title: Beyond frozen snapshots, protein 'breathing' comes into view with combined imaging methods
phys-org.description: Advances in structural biology have allowed scientists to determine molecular structures with atomic-level detail, sometimes yielding static snapshots that do not reflect the dynamism of proteins. However, these motions are often crucial for biological function. phys-org.title: AI schools like Alpha promise efficiency, but can't replicate the messy process that helps kids learn
phys-org.description: A child at a playground tries to climb, jump or negotiate with a peer, and the attempt does not work. They fall, get left out of a game or reach another impasse. Then they try again.

phys-org.title: Only 10 viral particles cause H5N1 avian flu infection in cows
phys-org.description: Just 10 viral particles of the H5N1 bird flu that caused hundreds of influenza outbreaks in U.S. dairy cattle can cause infection in cows, a new study shows. The research also hints at why the outbreaks have confounded scientists, farmers and livestock handlers hoping to contain and prevent the disease—an effort likely complicated by the fact that the virus has an affinity for cow mammary glands rather than airways.

phys-org.title: The 'right to repair' movement has a point, but consumers should read the warranty fine print first
phys-org.description: The "right to repair" movement is gaining steam as consumers push corporations to offer them more freedom to fix products—from cars to dishwashers to toys.

phys-org.title: Plants reveal backup system for sensing and adapting to rising temperatures
phys-org.description: University of Mississippi researchers are studying how plants respond to heat at the molecular level, an important consideration for farmers, businesses and policymakers as global temperatures rise.

phys-org.title: A star's death throes involve a lot of kicking
phys-org.description: When stars like our sun age, they puff up into red giants. Their bubbling outer mass gradually escapes into space, and their remaining cores contract into white dwarfs. Since most stars end their lives this way, the universe is teeming with white dwarfs. A new study from Caltech's Jim Fuller, professor of theoretical astrophysics, proposes a new model of the final death throes of sun-like stars that shows how escaping mass from the stars' surfaces leads to a series of little kicks.

phys-org.title: Global uncertainty is the new normal. Here's why institutional legitimacy and resilience are crucial
phys-org.description: The world has never had more data, more models or more economists. It has rarely felt more out of control. Uncertainty, not risk, has become the defining condition of our era. Central bankers invoke it. Political leaders use it to defer decisions and justify extraordinary ones. Academics are struggling to adapt their theories to a brave new world of unexpected outcomes and erratic policy choices. The IMF's World Uncertainty Index—which tracks how often the word appears in economic and polit

phys-org.title: Abstract algebra unlocks distinguishable states for quantum systems
phys-org.description: Researchers around the world are racing to develop new quantum-based systems for sensing, communication, computing and control that have the promise of outperforming traditional systems. Creating stable, measurable, distinguishable quantum states—which would be the heart of any such system—is a daunting task.

phys-org.title: Chandra reveals flickering supernova remnants in M83 over 14 years
phys-org.description: The aftermath of a supernova, a stellar explosion, is usually a slowly fading cloud of hot gas. So when astronomers pointed NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory at the nearby galaxy Messier 83 (M83), they did not expect to find a population of supernova remnants, or the debris from these explosions, showing dramatic changes in their brightness. The new results have been presented at the American Astronomical Society meeting in Pasadena, California, and published in The Astrophysical Journal.

phys-org.title: Digital platforms are making it more difficult to focus, read and even engage in democracy
phys-org.description: Oxford's 2024 Word of the Year, "brain rot," refers to the loss of intelligence or critical thinking skills due to the overconsumption of specific types of content, most often in the digital sphere. A Binghamton University doctoral student has published findings that help explain how the structural forces of large tech companies make it difficult to focus, read and even engage in democracy.

phys-org.title: Thermochemical mantle plume identified as the likely origin of Earth's largest oceanic plateau
phys-org.description: The Ontong Java Plateau in the western Pacific Ocean is the largest oceanic plateau on Earth, and its formation mechanism has not been well understood.

phys-org.title: Feeling poorer than peers linked to lower well-being, even when incomes are similar
phys-org.description: New research is shedding light on how comparing ourselves to others affects happiness and life satisfaction. Led by McGill University researchers, the study shows that people who feel worse off financially than their peers are more likely to report signs of languishing, even when their actual income is similar. The paper is published in the journal Social Science & Medicine.

phys-org.title: Modern human skeletal biology needs to move beyond the strict male/female binary, scientists argue

While analytical methods portray skeletal sex differences as almost purely binary (female or male), a person's sex—including hormones, genetics, external anatomy, internal anatomy and the skel

phys-org.title: Deep Earth model traces 270 million years of seamount formation across oceans
phys-org.description: Over 40,000 seamounts—undersea mountains that don't breach the ocean's surface—are scattered across the ocean floor. Some form linear chains, while others occur as dispersed, isolated features that are not part of well-defined volcanic chains.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

proj-syn.title: India’s Unfinished Reform Agenda
proj-syn.description: Elevated oil prices, potentially strong El Niño conditions during the monsoon season, and the tariff-induced fragmentation of global trade are bearing down on the Indian economy and will likely be a drag on GDP growth. But these adverse conditions may be a blessing in disguise if they force India to complete its economic reform agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Middle East’s New Normal
proj-syn.description: The most likely outcome of the Iran war is not peace but an unsatisfying ceasefire that leaves the underlying issues unresolved. This will mean an uneasy equilibrium in which Gulf countries go their own way, US influence wanes, and the regional order remains unsettled.

proj-syn.title: No Bridge Over Healing Waters for the G7
proj-syn.description: The French G7 presidency’s focus on global imbalances is both welcome and problematic. While long-standing trade imbalances between the United States, Europe, and China are, if anything, becoming even more troublesome, the leaders’ summit in Évian-les-Bains will do nothing to address the problem.

proj-syn.title: Are Government Stakes the Key to AI Sovereignty?
proj-syn.description: At first glance, reports that the US and Chinese governments are both considering taking stakes in national AI champions would seem to suggest a convergence between the world’s two leading AI powers. But a closer look reveals stark differences in their underlying strategies.

proj-syn.title: From the American Revolution to Universal Suffrage
proj-syn.description: Britain’s attempt to crush the American Revolution exposed a constitutional crisis at the heart of its empire. One English statesman saw in it proof that only broader suffrage could check royal power, tame corruption, and ensure that imperial rule remained compatible with liberty.

proj-syn.title: Jefferson’s Revolutionary Language
proj-syn.description: Of the delegates who assembled in Philadelphia in 1776 for the Second Continental Congress, only Thomas Jefferson possessed the skill, knowledge, and linguistic gifts to make the Declaration of Independence an immortal text. He was the self-appointed conscience of America, and sensational imagery was his stock-in-trade.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of the Enslaved
proj-syn.description: For African-Americans, the Declaration of Independence was nothing but a “thin veil to cover the crimes” of slavery, as Frederick Douglass put it. Inspired by Haiti’s Declaration of Independence, free and enslaved Black people in the US found themselves subverting America’s founding document to achieve their own emancipation.

proj-syn.title: Free-Market Capitalism Is Destroying US Democracy
proj-syn.description: Far from two sides of the same coin, free-market capitalism and democracy are fundamentally incompatible. The only way to restore US democracy is to transform the system, so that it compensates innovators but limits their market power, while ensuring that the benefits of economic progress are more equitably shared.

proj-syn.title: Canada’s Great Recalibration
proj-syn.description: The growing fusion of economics, security, and technology has altered the nature of 21st-century interdependence, and Canada has responded by being more intentional. Rather than automatically serving as an extension of US-centered systems, it is creating more options across a wider network of relationships.

proj-syn.title: From Jefferson to Nehru
proj-syn.description: The Declaration of Independence continues to challenge countries, including the US and India, to measure themselves against the ideals they profess. But in a century marked by rising inequality, an authoritarian resurgence, and the emergence of new forms of domination, measuring up will become only more difficult.

proj-syn.title: The Roots of Democratic Decline
proj-syn.description: Notwithstanding recent setbacks for illiberal, populist, and authoritarian leaders in some countries, good-governance groups and experts on democratic decline continue to document a disturbing global trend toward “autocratization.” What remains to be seen is whether enough voters will wake up to the threat.

proj-syn.title: The Standard of Independence
proj-syn.description: Although revolutions would surely have occurred had the United States never broken from Britain in 1776, the Declaration of Independence gave later anticolonial movements inspiration and the language to shape their own aspirations. It offered a universal blueprint, even as the US itself adopted the ethos of empire.

proj-syn.title: The Declaration of Independence Turns South
proj-syn.description: Whether they were agreeing or arguing, the new countries that emerged across the Americas after the American Revolution influenced each other. Together, they helped shape the global development of modern democracy and the social and political movements that have shaped it ever since.

proj-syn.title: Capitalism’s Creature
proj-syn.description: The American Dream, with its basis in Thomas Jefferson’s immortal words, was one of the most powerfully generative ideas ever conceived. But the economy and impersonal systems it helped to bring into being are now shaping society and its individual members, rather than the other way around.

proj-syn.title: What the Declaration Did and Did Not Say
proj-syn.description: The American founders’ understanding of political community was ethnically and racially restrictive in ways that Americans have since repudiated. But the Declaration of Independence’s underlying logic and treatment of rights and what it takes to secure them remains as cogent as it was 250 years ago.

proj-syn.title: Independence for Me, But Not for Thee
proj-syn.description: The Declaration of Independence spoke of all states as being "separate and equal," reflecting the founders' deference to the norms of international law and practice. Yet 250 years later, Donald Trump's administration has inverted this posture, much to the detriment of America's standing in the world.

proj-syn.title: China’s AI Agenda
proj-syn.description: While American and international news coverage of AI tends to focus on a handful of Silicon Valley labs, China's more pragmatic approach to leveraging the technology could ultimately be the bigger story. What the Chinese leadership sees in the technology is nothing less than a master key for its economic ambitions.
